Show HN: Skjalf TV, Steam Deck native, controller-first IPTV player
items.summary: I wanted to watch my IPTV subscription on the Steam Deck, both handheld and docked to a TV. But any existing option was either a desktop app or a Kodi setup (or worse, an Android emulator setup) that fought with Game Mode, so I wrote a player that treats the Deck as the main target. It is purposefully simple. It plays live TV, movies, and series from your own Xtream Codes account or M3U playlist. It ships no channels or content. items.title: Show HN: ChineseHuangli: A modern spin of traditional Chinese almanac calendar
items.summary: The Chinese almanac calendar has been around for centuries. It is normally for the older generation. The do's and don'ts cover things like building a house, chopping trees, hunting or fishing. I think it is fun to adapt it to modern activities such as dating, software releases, and parties. You can add your own activities and check which day is good for them. It explains why some activities are favored or not, tracing back to ancient books. Show HN: A minimal internet radio inspired by Dieter Rams
items.summary: When my Beoplay A1 speaker died, I reused its driver to build the radio I'd been missing: turn a knob and the music plays. It has a station selector and a VFD, with no touchscreen and no app. The software is in Rust and runs on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. It has machined aluminium plates and a walnut housing I built with a woodworker in Sweden. Software (MIT), drawings and plate files: https://github.com/laibe/cala-radio
items.company: minimal internet radio inspired by Dieter Rams

items.title: Show HN: Turn any selfie into a 3D head you can stretch like Mario 64
items.summary: Floppy Face is an app I built that transforms any selfie photo into a 3D head you can pull and stretch like the opening of Mario 64. The app runs on Three.js and WebGL, so it performs smoothly on a browser or phone. When a photo is uploaded, Floppy Face uses MediaPipe to detect facial landmarks and map them onto a 468-point face template with estimated depth. The mesh is then subdivided for smoother stretching. Show HN: Doom inside a 39M-parameter neural network
items.summary: Code: https://github.com/kulikov0/micro-doom-world Weights: https://huggingface.co/kulikov0/micro-doom-world A 39M-parameter diffusion transformer predicts the next 128x96 frame from the previous 31 frames and the keys you press. It runs in the browser on WebGPU (it was tested on chrome and safari, I'm not sure how it runs in other browsers). Trained it on 1.5M frames of a scripted bot playing freedoom E1M1-E1M3. Note: it won't run well on every device. On my M4 Max it's smooth, but on a Pixel I get only 1-2 fps because of the hardware. Without WebGPU it falls back to CPU and it's very slow
